findings.issue: TIMING6/7 CPU-DDR; synthesized CDC unknown nodes
findings.actual_path: CPU/MMIO/IOMMU/iDMA memory traffic crosses asynchronous AXI converter and DDR PHY; reset crosses CPU/MIG UI domains
findings.positive_evidence: Known asynchronous converter, three synchronization stages; routed Gray pointer max-delay5ns slack4.238ns; CPU-reset to MIG positive reported slack but dependent on original clock definition. IP-specific reset/dual-clock-memory waivers exist.
findings.identity: Successful bounded read is an actual observation, not full CDC proof.
findings.ordinary: Finite raw functional capture may enter after other root gates, with complete bytes/hardware completion/error/reset records for the same boot. Do not accept remaining unknown nodes as waived solely from synthesis summary.
findings.stronger_claim_minimum: Classify active CPU-DDR unknown endpoints against actual IP ownership, applied constraints/waivers and reset/handshake structure, or obtain corrected clock-ancestry path acceptance; no automatic whole-board rebuild.

findings.issue: TIMING6/7 CPU-TCK and partial JTAG input delays
findings.actual_path: Soft CPU DMI request/response CDC; distinct from native configuration TAP
findings.identity: UART/Linux mode read needs no DMI request. CPU tck100ns constraint is not evidence of native JTAG physical clock.
findings.ordinary: No DMI request/halt/reset/reconfiguration in measured restore window; release task-owned debug access. If DMI is used to observe status/time, this crossing becomes active and requires handshake/timing evidence.

findings.issue: DDR PHY input/output missing ordinary delay
findings.actual_path: ddr3_dqs_p0..3 and ddr3_reset_n; all restoration memory traffic uses DDR
findings.identity: Missing ordinary IO delays do not by themselves establish a failed calibrated MIG interface.
findings.ordinary: Entire restored payload comparison, documented hardware completion and observed error/reset checks provide finite run correctness. Record calibration/lock only if existing live interfaces expose it; native CONFIG_STATUS PLL bit is not a direct MIG calibration observation.
findings.not_proven: One successful run and IP PHY/reset constraints are not complete board-level DDR IO timing acceptance.

findings.issue: Ethernet/UART external IO and Ethernet unsafe CDC categories
findings.actual_path: control, upload/readback, result collection; possible memory traffic during the restore window
findings.identity: Require complete parsed fields and correct magic/version/schema. A mismatch stops interpretation; clock warnings are not a diagnosis of the mismatch.
findings.ordinary: Record real transfer/verification results. Preparatory transport and result retrieval may be staged separately but all actual time/CPU/copy/resource costs remain charged. Traffic inside the memory measurement window is an explicit participant; dropped/corrupted transport cannot be interpreted as translation cost.
findings.stronger_claim_minimum: For network-timing/causal results, classify active Ethernet endpoints and external RGMII timing; UART-only functional observation does not require signoff of unused network traffic.

findings.actual_path: LED/fan/switch GPIO; SD SPI used at boot or explicitly if scenario uses it; clock/reset continuity
findings.identity: Do not delay identity read for unused indicator timing. Actual boot is finite functional evidence for its boot path.
findings.ordinary: If no SD write/read in restore data path, SPI does not gate that path; boot/delivery costs still recorded. If SD forms part of restoration, actual IO completion/data verification required. Reset/unlock/reboot invalidates same-boot interval accounting.
